title: JRE 2320 - Tom Segura
guestBio: Tom Segura is a stand-up comedian, actor, podcaster, and author. He co-hosts two podcasts: “Your Mom’s House” with his wife, comedian Christina Pazsitzky, and “Two Bears, One Cave” with Bert Kreischer. He is also the author of “I’d Like to Play Alone, Please: Essays.” Watch his comedy series, “Bad Thoughts,” now streaming on Netflix.
tldr: Tom Segura and Joe catch up on the current state of stand-up comedy and what has changed in the touring landscape since Tom's last appearance
Discussion of YMH Studios and how Tom and Christina built a podcast network into one of the most successful independent comedy media companies
Tom breaks down his approach to writing and developing stand-up specials and why he keeps the creative process close to the chest until it is ready
Conversation about his expanding acting career and the projects he has been focused on outside of stand-up and podcasting
Joe and Tom on the comedy community, road friendships, and the shared experience of performing for massive crowds across the country
Tom shares what still drives him to keep writing and touring when he could easily coast on his existing success and catalog
recap: Without access to the complete transcript, a detailed recap cannot be accurately generated. However, this episode features Tom Segura, one of comedy's most prolific voices, sitting down with Joe Rogan for what is typically a long-form conversation covering comedy, podcasting, and his creative projects. Tom is known for his observational humor and willingness to go deep on topics ranging from the absurd to the personal. He co-hosts Your Mom's House with his wife Christina Pazsitzky, which has become one of the most popular comedy podcasts, and also hosts Two Bears One Cave with Bert Kreischer. Beyond podcasting, Tom has established himself as a serious stand-up with multiple specials and is constantly touring. His Netflix series Bad Thoughts showcases his comedic sensibility across scripted content. When Tom comes on JRE, the conversation typically flows naturally between his current projects, observations about comedy and the industry, and the kind of casual deep-dives into random topics that make the podcast format work so well. Tom brings a sharp sense of humor and genuine curiosity to conversations, which tends to make for engaging episodes.
